name: Kṛṣṇa (Vāsudeva)
summary: In BhG 7–9 the speaker ('śrī bhagavān uvāca'); he names himself Vāsudeva (7.19) and is addressed by Arjuna as Puruṣottama (8.1) and Madhusūdana (8.2). He teaches his two natures, the world's delusion by his guṇa-made māyā, remembrance of him at death, the two paths of the departing, his sovereign yoga, and undivided devotion to him.

name: Arjuna (Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya)
summary: Addressee of BhG 7–9; his only speech in these chapters is the set of questions at 8.1–2 (what are brahman, adhyātma, karma, adhibhūta, adhidaiva; who is the adhiyajña in the body; how the Lord is known at the time of departure).
